why_824_and_not_825: The live tree holds 825 by discover()'s rule -- one more than the triaged run, because b18 added tests/run_window_anchor_ratchet_probe.py AFTER the run started. The pin is set to what the TRIAGED RUN MEASURED, not to the current count: a floor is `count >= pin`, so 824 is the conservative direction and the ratchet raises it to 825 on the next full-tree run. Setting a pin above what the run saw would be pinning a number nothing has verified.

Another clone raised 808 -> 811 from its own run and pushed while cody b18's 808 -> 824 sat unpushed, so the rebase conflicted on this file. 824 > 811, the floor only rises, and 824 is the number a TRIADED full-tree run measured -- so 824 stands and `previous` now reads 811, which is what this pin actually replaced. the_generator_drops_keys_it_does_not_kno: READ THIS BEFORE WRITING ANOTHER EXPLANATORY KEY HERE. The 811 version of this file arrived with `lowered_from_813_why` ABSENT -- not deleted by a person, dropped by tools/run_all_tests.py raise_floor(), which rewrites the file from its own fixed key set. So every hand-written key in this file, including the four above, survives only until the next full-tree run raises the pin. That is why the b14 lowering note is restored here rather than left gone: the one operation this ratchet forbids is a lowering, and the record of the time it happened is exactly what a generator should not be able to silently discard. The durable place for any of this is a commit message or a docs/ file; this one is a cache of the latest reason.
